title: Define acceptance matrix for tiered SLOs, probe sampling, and canary exit criteria
creator: Lina Patel
description: Purpose: Create a clear, executable acceptance matrix that ties tiered SLO definitions to concrete probe sampling rules, canary probe pass/fail thresholds, and automated exit criteria for progressive rollouts across hosted and dedicated deployments. This ticket defines the product-level requirements and acceptance criteria so engineering and SRE can implement metrics collection, probe sampling, and the rollout gating logic in the control plane.
background: We already have high-level SLO targets and multiple tickets about storefront and tenant SLOs, but teams lack a single, testable acceptance matrix that maps observed metrics (p50/p95/p99 latency, availability, and error budgets) to canary behavior (hold, promote, rollback) and measurement sampling cadence. Recent canaries exposed inconsistent probe configurations between Hosted and Dedicated, creating noisy false positives and manual escalations.
goals: Produce an acceptance matrix that maps SLO tier -> metric signals -> probe sampling configuration -> explicit canary exit conditions
Standardize probe types (synthetic single-token latency probe, multi-turn chat probe, embedding throughput probe) and sampling cadence for each SLO tier
Define automated canary exit rules (promote/hold/rollback) with burn-rate style rules and minimum probe window
Provide example PromQL queries / SQL for measurement so the runtime team can implement circuit logic and console can surface gate status
non_goals: Implementing the runtime gating automation (engineering tickets will follow),
Changing SLO numeric targets — this ticket references proposed targets but final targets are set by SRE/PM leadership
Per-tenant custom probes — this defines global defaults and per-tier overrides only
proposed_slos: Tier A (premium): p99 inference latency <= 200ms, availability >= 99.95%, error budget 0.05% per 30d
Tier B (standard): p99 inference latency <= 400ms, availability >= 99.9%, error budget 0.1% per 30d
Tier C (best-effort): p99 inference latency <= 800ms, availability >= 99.5%, error budget 0.5% per 30d
Note: For streaming chat the p95 first-token latency targets are 80% of the p99 target above for each tier
probe_definitions: latency-probe/single-token: simple POST to /v1/completions with fixed prompt and model, measure time-to-first-byte; sample cadence: Tier A=10s, Tier B=30s, Tier C=2m

chat-smoke: 3-turn deterministic chat conversation with fixed user messages & seed for deterministic response, measures end-to-end latency and response fidelity; cadence: Tier A=30s, Tier B=2m, Tier C=10m
embedding-throughput: batch embedding probe with 16 items to validate throughput and queueing; cadence: Tier A=1m, Tier B=5m, Tier C=15m
rollout_gates: Gate 0 - Pre-flight: unit/integration tests and canary config validated (manual)
Gate 1 - Warmup Window (satellite rollout): 5 minute probe window, no SLO breach and success rate >= 99.9% -> auto promote to canary

Gate 2 - Canary Evaluation: 30 minute window, burn-rate check across probes. Auto-promote if burn-rate <= 0.5 and p99 within 10% of target; hold and extend if inconclusive; rollback if burn-rate > 2.0 or availability breaches threshold
Gate 3 - Gradual Ramp: 4 step ramp (10%, 25%, 50%, 100%) with 15 minute steady-state observation per step and cumulative error budget consumption < 25% at each step
Gate 4 - Post-promote Ramp Monitoring: 24h observation with SLO alerting and rollback hooks if sustained degradation is detected
probe_sampling_and_windowing: Minimum probe count per evaluation window: Tier A=100 probes, Tier B=40 probes, Tier C=10 probes
If minimum probes not met due to low traffic, use synthetic probes at configured cadence. Do not make canary decisions with <50 samples for Tier A
Use sliding windows (exponential backoff) for initial canary vs fixed windows for ramp steps to avoid noisy spikes
measurement_queries: burn_rate: (errors_in_window / error_budget) over 30d scaled to window length; recommend using existing burn-rate library for consistency
acceptance_criteria: Product: Acceptance matrix document reviewed and approved by PM, SRE, Runtime, and Console leads
SRE: Measurement queries validated against staging telemetry (example dashboards show expected numbers for synthetic load)
Runtime: Probe SDK contract agreed (endpoint, headers, timeout semantics) and engineering ticket created to implement gating logic
Console: UI wireframe for canary status and per-gate pass/fail displayed in rollout page
QA: Synthetic probe harness in staging reproduces at least 3 failure modes and triggers expected rollbacks/promotion behavior
Documentation: Confluence page with step-by-step guide, example queries, and troubleshooting checklist
risks_and_mitigation: False positives from noisy probes -> mitigate with minimum probe counts, smoothing windows, and requiring multiple signals before rollback
Cross-region variance causing canary flakiness -> require region-consistent metrics and add regional gates
Probe-induced load affecting real customers -> cap synthetic probe QPS and isolate in dedicated capacity during canaries
Ambiguous error classification (5xx vs client errors) -> standardize error label set and require runtime changes to surface error_reason
